REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES
  MAY 24, 2021

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:01 p.m.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Silvano, Shinn, Ciarolla, Robinson, Griggs, Harik,

Committee Members Absent:  Brtis, Martin, Nilsen, Zigrang

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor, Cynthia Morquecho

DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 26, 2021

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO, to:

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE APRIL 26, 2021, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF so ordered.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

None.

STAFF ITEMS

  A. COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis stated that COVID case numbers continue to decline. Less restrictions as the County
is now in the yellow tier. Vaccination rates for Rolling Hills Estates is above 70%. All areas will be
reopened on June 15, 2021 per State’s reopening guidance. The City will be moving forward with
businesses and events reopening to full capacity under protocols as determined. The City will
await direction from the State and County for guidance on mask wearing.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  B. DEDICATION BENCH AND PLAQUE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief review of the status of the proposed dedication plaque
for retired trainer Jan Ball and Equestrian Carol Dean Porter. Staff reported that the approved
plaque application submitted by the Equestrian Committee was approved and staff has requested
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  1
MAY 24, 2021
 a quote for the bench, plaque, and installation with a total $1,422 for the bench with attached
plaque. The plaque for Carol Dean Porter has been quoted for $432.00. Additionally, $310 has
been received to date. Staff requested that equestrian members consider seeking donations to
help fund the two recognitions.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  C. TRAIL RIDING OPERATION PERMIT REVIEW

ACM Davis provided a brief review of the staff report.

Community Member Nancy Zinner stated that trail riding operation utilizes the area located
behind her residence and she has encountered a high level of noise being generated from the
group. CHAIR HUFF asked for letters of concern received be read to the public and entered for
the record.

Community Member Joe Washko stated that as a longtime resident of Rolling Hills Estates, the
trail riding operation that is currently conducting business has become a very big issue and has
negatively impacted his property value. CHAIR HUFF thanked the public for their feedback on
the issue and asked that the Committee consider how to work with Palos Verdes Estates Stables
on relocating the starting point for the trail riding business. ACM Davis stated that the City has
contacted the City of Palos Verdes Estates and is working to resolve the issue. Additionally, the
City of Palos Verdes Estates does review approved Conditional Uses on an annual basis, but it
was not completed in 2020. The City of Palos Verdes Estates will be taking the issue to their
Planning Commission for review. CHAIR HUFF stated that although the Committee is supportive
of the equestrian activity, she is also concerned for the needs of the residents.

MEMBER SHINN stated that the issues being brought to the Committee sound like two separate
issues: with one being related to the business being in compliant to the polices of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates trail use, and the second issue being a noise complaint that should be
handled by the City of Palos Verdes Estates. ACM Davis responded that the City of Rolling Hills
Estates is helping to advocate for Rolling Hills Estates residents on the issue and staff is coming
to the Committee on the issue of upholding City policy for a business license and horse permit.
Staff is providing the Committee with a list of conditions that the trail riding company must adhere
to in order to maintain a valid business license and use City trails. MEMBER HARIK stated that
a good resolution would be to move the starting point of the trail ride to a location away from
Rolling Hills Estates residences. MEMBER SILVANO stated that she is excited to hear that there
is so much interest in trail riding and feels that it is important to keep the City trails be available
for use. CHAIR HUFF agreed with the sentiment and restated that the issue is not with the trail
use but with the disturbance to the City residents.

MEMBER GRIGGS stated that she is directly impacted by the noise generated from the trail riding
operation and suggested establishing a starting location within PV stables and utilizing only the
Palos Verdes Estate’s Trails. MEMBER SILVANO stated that it might be an issue to be
exclusionary with City trails and that setting conditions may be a more ideal solution. CHAIR
HUFF suggested requiring smaller groups for the trail ride. MEMBER SILVANO asked if the
maximum requirement will be implemented across the board. MEMBER GRIGGS responded that
the issue is that the trail rides are taking place every half hour.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  2
MAY 24, 2021
 CHAIR HUFF stated that a letter from the Rolling Hills Estates City Council or City Manager
should encourage the City of Palos Verdes Estates to move their trail riding operation to a
different location. MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if the trails for Palos Verdes Estates are still
accessible considering so many trails in their City have been closed. ACM Davis stated that they
understand that some groups were riding out to Ernie Howlett and Chandler Park and is unsure
of the reasoning behind use of Rolling Hills Estates trails. ACM Davis provided an overview of
the draft list of conditions for the Committees review and input. CHAIR HUFF clarified that the
conditions provided is specific to this trail riding operation.

MEMBER ROBINSON stated that the starting time may be too early and should be moved to
later considering that the operation must unload horses earlier in the morning, which could disturb
neighboring residences. CHAIR HUFF added that the start time is especially early for Sunday
mornings. MEMBER SILVANO suggested the last ride commence no later than 4:00 pm. She
added that the increase in use of the trail riding operation may be in part due to COVID and not
having many outdoor activity options. MEMBER ROBINSON suggested a start time no earlier
than 10:00 am Monday through Saturday and 11:00 am on Sundays, and added that Palos
Verdes Estates should consider moving the starting location. MEMBER GRIGGS stated that she
has seen several riders fall off a horse with no helmet on. ACM Davis stated that the conditions
will include all patrons will be required to wear a helmet.

Additionally, staff would like include the condition of manure removal from excess trail use which
could adversely impact the storm water safety requirements. MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if
residents will be required to clean up after their horses and is concerned that manure removal by
the permit holder does not seem like an enforceable requirement to be implemented. MEMBER
ROBINSON asked if the requirement would be enforced while using a hitching post or walking
through the park and trails. ACM Davis responded that it would be required for both. ACM Davis
stated that the permit applicant asked for the ability to host Full Moon rides once a month. CHAIR
HUFF stated that if the business continues to use the current location the Committee may want
to consider a time limit for a full moon ride. MEMBER GRIGGS added that PV stables is required
to shut off lights at 9:00pm. MEMBER SIVLANO suggested not allowing full moon rides at this
time and reconsider if the starting point location is moved.

MEMBER HARIK asked how much money PV stables is making from the trail riding operation.
Community Member Zinner asked if the trail ride operation has a current business license. ACM
Davis responded that they do not have a current business license with the City of Rolling Hills
Estates. The City of Rolling Hills Estates started communication with the owner in the fall of 2020.
CHAIR HUFF clarified that the rental owner was under the impression that he was a Palos Verdes
Estates business and he understood that the business only required approval from the City of
Palos Verdes Estates.

Community Member Schachter asked how the conditions would be enforced. ACM Davis stated
that code enforcement is available throughout the week and on some weekends and would look
to enforce the conditions as needed. Community Member Washko stated that efforts have been
made ask for a relocation of the horse rental starting location and the operator has not indicated
that they are open to moving the starting location of the business. She expressed concerns with
the Palos Verdes Estates Conditional Use Permit process and stated it is unfortunate that the
City of Rolling Hills Estates is considering allowing a business that is disturbing the residence to
continue operating within City limits. She further stated that the City of Rolling Hills Estates should
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  3
MAY 24, 2021
 consider allowing the trail riding operation to operate out a City facility; the City of Palos Verdes
Estates has closed many of their trails and does not accommodate the City of Rolling Hills
Estates.

CHAIR HUFF stated that staff will continue to work with the City of Palos Verdes Estates to
mitigate the issue. ACM Davis asked for clarification on how many rides occur within operating
hours.

MEMBER HARIK asked what the authority is to deny the business license. ACM Davis stated
that the City is limited in denying the permit and license unless the operator does not comply with
the conditions set. MEMBER ROBINSON asked if the conditions could be more restrictive. ACM
Davis stated that the conditions would have to be reasonable but can be set to mitigate any
concerns of the community and City. CHAIR HUFF suggested revisiting the noise ordinances as
additional way to mitigate the issue.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report for the conditions to be
modified to include:

  •  Start time no earlier than 10:00 am Monday through Friday and 11:00 am Sunday.
  •  Full Moon Rides will not be allowed.

  D. HORSE SHOW AND SPECIAL EVENTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Morquecho stated that as the County moves through the tier system, restrictions have
been loosened on group gatherings and events. Currently, the County has opened up for group
gatherings of up to 100 people, which has allowed for the City to open to horse shows. Staff
continues to discuss with County representatives the upcoming changes to events as we are
looking to move into the yellow tier. Additionally, the County may be removing all restrictions by
mid-June. Some of the City Annual events have been postponed including the Tracy Austin
Tournament, and Mayor’s Breakfast Ride. Additionally, the Hills Are Alive event will be held on
August 7, 2021 for an in person race.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  E. EQUESTRIAN LOG

MEMBER SHINN stated that Superintendent Goldsmith is always available and completes any
work necessary in a timely manner.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF received and filed the report.

  F. FOURTH OF JULY SAFETY UPDATE

ACM Davis provided an overview of the mitigation efforts that will take place leading up to the 4th
of July Holiday. Items included closing landfill early, coordination with the Sheriff’s Department,
information out to city residents, message alerts and social media blasts. MEMBER SHINN stated
that 7:00pm would be a good time to close the landfill early. Additionally, it should be considered

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  4
MAY 24, 2021
 to hire an off-duty guard to monitor the trails. Due to the high rate of fire issues it is important to
consider the safety of the City and the fire concern.

Community Member Schacter asked if the Sheriff’s Posse might be available to patrol the trails
on the evening of Fourth of July. ACM Davis responded that the question has been asked of the
Sheriff’s Posse, but due to COVID and other considerations unfortunately the Posse is
unavailable. MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the access point from Crenshaw to the Landfill would
be closed early as well. City staff will assess that access road and will reach out to the Sheriff’s
Department.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A.  ADOPT-A- TRAIL

None.

  B.  CHANDLER PARK UPDATE

Supervisor Morquecho stated that after the review of the playground proposal the subcommittee
could not come to a clear consensus on the recommendation on how to proceed. Therefore, the
subcommittee would not be providing a recommendation to the Park and Activities Commission.
CHAIR HUFF clarified that the location of the proposed playground should be discussed with the
Commission.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A. COMMITTEE T-SHIRTS
B. YOUTH AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR HUFF ADJOURNED THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING 8:36 pm

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

Cynthia Morquecho  __________________________
Community Services Supervisor  Britt Huff, Chair

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES  5
MAY 24, 2021
